- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.2) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward → reduce forecast peak by 5–10% in next 5–7 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +10% above recent high), model often overshoots → cap forecast at +5% above prior peak for next 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (avg > -0.1) and price is trending down, model often fails to recognize mean reversion → adjust downward by 2–4% per day until sentiment shifts.  
- When sentiment turns sharply positive (e.g., > +0.3) after a downtrend, model often overreacts → reduce forecast slope by 10–15% for next 7 days.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price drops in 30-day horizon when sentiment is negative → add 1–2% buffer to forecast for next 5 days if sentiment remains negative.  
- If sentiment is volatile (±0.3 or more) and price is flat, model often overfits noise → smooth forecast by averaging 3–5 prior days’ values before projecting.
